elements.id-string-12: \vspace{1cm}The spin-$\nicefrac{3}{2}$ to spin-$\nicefrac{1}{2}$ doubly heavy baryon transition magnetic dipole $G_M$ and electric quadrupole $G_E$ formfactors are calculated in the framework of light cone sum rules method.
elements.id-string-13: Moreover, the decay widths of corresponding radiative transitions are estimated.
elements.id-string-14: Obtained results of magnetic dipole moments $G_M$ and decay widths are compared with the results present in the literature.
elements.id-string-15: \keywords{light-cone QCD sum rules, doubly heavy baryons, electromagnetic transitions}
elements.id-string-17: The quark model predicts the existence of baryons containing two heavy quarks.
elements.id-string-18: The doubly heavy baryons constitute an important and promising system to study the structure of physics of a system containing two heavy quarks as well as for understanding the strong interaction at the non-perturbative domain.
elements.id-string-19: Doubly heavy baryons lie on the focus of theoretical and experimental investigations.
elements.id-string-20: Experimentally, the first observation of doubly heavy baryon $\Xi_{cc}^+$ was reported by SELEX Collaboration \cite{xi+}.
elements.id-string-21: The existence of its iso doublet partner $\Xi_{cc}^{++}$ state was observed by LHCb Collaboration in the $\Lambda_c^+K^-\pi^+\pi^+$ spectrum, with the mass $m_{\Xi_{cc}^{++}}=3621.40\pm0.72\pm0.14$ $MeV$ \cite{xi++}.
elements.id-string-22: The mass of $\Xi_{cc}^+$ has been updated in \cite{xi++,aaij2,aaij3,aaij4}.
elements.id-string-23: In the upgraded experiments planned at LHCb with large data samples additional states predicted by the quark model and new decay channels of doubly heavy baryons may be observed.
elements.id-string-24: The tremendous experimental developments triggered theoretical studies on the physics of doubly heavy baryons.
elements.id-string-25: Mainly the theoretical studies are concentrated on studying the mass, electromagnetic properties, and weak decays of doubly heavy baryons.
elements.id-string-26: These studies are critical to understanding the flavor structure and dynamics of these baryons.
elements.id-string-27: The mass of doubly charmed baryons within different approaches has been studied in many works such as constituent quark model \cite{consQM1,consQM2,consQM3,consQM4,consQM5,consQM6,consQM8,consQM9}, Regge phenomenology \cite{regge1,regge2}, QCD sum rules method \cite{qcdsr1,qcdsr2,qcdsr3,qcdsr4,AlievOctet,AlievDecuplet} and relativistic quark model\cite{rqm1}.
elements.id-string-28: The magnetic moment is another important quantity in studying the inner structure of hadrons.
elements.id-string-29: The magnetic moment of doubly charmed baryons within different approaches such as the  quark model, chiral perturbation theory, bag model, effective quark mass scheme, lattice QCD and harmonic oscillator model are calculated in \cite{transition15}, \cite{transition10}, \cite{DhirEMS}, \cite{exBag}, \cite{lattice} and \cite{harmonic} respectively.
elements.id-string-30: The spin-$\nicefrac{3}{2}$ to spin-$\nicefrac{1}{2}$ doubly heavy baryon transition magnetic moments receive special attention as it probes the inner structure as well as possible deformation of heavy baryons.
elements.id-string-31: In the present work, we calculate the transition magnetic moments of doubly heavy baryons with spin-$\nicefrac{3}{2}$ to spin-$\nicefrac{1}{2}$ within the light cone QCD sum rules (LCSR).

elements.id-string-35: In \textbf{section III} we present our numerical results on magnetic moments of considered transitions.
